articles.title: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
articles.summary: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.

articles.title: Inside the New York ‘time machine’ racing to save a century of sound and film
articles.summary: “I tell my kids I work in a time machine,” said Rhony Dostaly. In a basement beneath Lincoln Center, the media preservation engineer rescues moments from the past. “I go back in time, and I grab elements, and I make them available for people today.”

articles.title: COP17: The world has a plan to save nature. Is it working?
articles.summary: The UN Secretary-General has called for an end to the “war on nature”. On Monday, governments gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, will have to confront a more practical question: are they doing enough to win the peace and put the world’s biodiversity goals back on track?

articles.title: As disasters mount, next UN climate summit faces a test of trust
articles.summary: Less than a month before the UN climate conference COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye, representatives of three successive summit presidencies gathered to address a pressing question: How can the world restore trust in climate action when the consequences of a warming planet are already being felt?

articles.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology
articles.summary: Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court, according to a new UN report which warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights.

articles.title: Haiti sanctions renewed: Starving the gangs of bullets
articles.summary: Haiti is living through one of the world’s most acute security crises. Armed gangs control large parts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and are pushing into rural areas, terrorising communities, killing people, committing rape and other sexual assaults, kidnapping for ransom and extorting individuals and businesses.

articles.title: Yemen: Houthi siege, cholera outbreak and aid cuts put civilians in the crosshairs
articles.summary: Yemen’s southwestern city of Taiz is facing a “devastating” humanitarian crisis as escalating tensions are dramatically driving up food prices and causing shortages of supplies, the UN Spokesperson said on Tuesday.
